rows.title: Transporter tab: transporters listed with approval number and type, and filtered by type
rows.detail: Once it is decided that the address book manages transporters, the address book list gains a Transporter tab between 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', headed 'Transporter addresses', with its own columns (Name, Address, Approval number and Type) and a Type filter of 'Commercial' and 'Private', so a trader can see and narrow the organisation's transporters in the same place as its other addresses. It is blocked with the rest of transporter management: nobody has decided whether the service manages transporters at all, or, if it does, whether the address book or something else does.
acceptanceCriteria: The address book list shows a 'Transporter' tab between 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', headed 'Transporter addresses', holding the organisation's addresses of the transporter type (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-022 to prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-006, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-031; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-088, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-097)
Such an address's Type column reads 'Transporter' on the tabs that show a Type column (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-031)

On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the action column with no visible heading; the address's last line carries the country, an approval number reads in the form 'RO/BUCHAREST/T1/00092010', and Type reads 'Commercial' or 'Private' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-031, prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-036; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-032 to trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-035, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-132; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p6-098)

On the Transporter tab the Type filter offers 'Select one', 'Commercial' and 'Private', and the list it returns holds, across the whole category and filtered on the server, every transporter whose transporter type equals the choice (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-017; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-024; repo:addressbook repo-addressbook-p3-046)
With Welsh selected, the Transporter tab, its heading, its column headings and its Type filter options show their Welsh copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-045)

sources.ref: repo-addressbook-p3-046 (the list API filters on q and countryCode only, with no type filter)
ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-031 to p2-035, p2-041, p2-043, p2-045 (transporter management blocked; the Transporter tab, its columns and its Welsh wait)

openQuestions: The product owner decides whether the service manages transporters and, if so, whether in the address book (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm, transporter management, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-031 to p2-035, p2-041, p2-043); the transporter area is then re-distilled and this row rewritten to that decision. No safe default: a Transporter tab with no transporter entries behind it would show an empty, unreachable category.
rows.notes: Combines the Transporter tab (req-2040), its columns (req-1135) and its Type filter (req-2041): one tab, one blocker, one set-up. Rewrite of the existing blocked row inc-075, keeping its id. Still blocked: the 26 October ruling says nothing about transporters, so ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm's block stands, and this re-distil only restates the requirements and renumbers the afternoon ruling's claims. Two changes from the existing row's text: its 'Search on the Transporter tab finds a transporter by part of its approval number' criterion is dropped, because no requirement here states it and the search requirement it leaned on (req-1119, held by the address-book split) matches on name, type labels, address lines and country name, not on an approval number; and 'with no Country column' is replaced by naming the four columns and the action column exactly, which proves the same thing positively. Whether a transporter's approval number becomes searchable is for the re-distil after the transporter decision. The category and type query parameter names are the INS service's to choose, so no criterion names one. Waits on the address book split branch's tabs and search rows (externalDependsOn on shared/design-release-2-1/themes/address-book inc-067 and inc-069) and on the add-a-transporter row.

rows.title: Transporter is one of the address types offered when adding an address
rows.detail: Once it is decided that the address book manages transporters, the address types a trader chooses from when adding an address include 'Transporter', so a transporter can be added to the book alongside the other parties. It is blocked with the rest of transporter management: offering the type with nowhere to add a transporter leads nowhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding an address offers the address type 'Transporter', after 'Place of Destination' and before the divider, with the hint 'This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p15-110; repo:tests repo-tests-p5-095; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-044)

rows.title: The address book list filters as the trader types, once design answers
rows.detail: With JavaScript, the address book list re-requests itself as the trader types in the search field or changes the Type select, after a short pause, and swaps in the table, the results line and the pagination without a full page load, so a trader narrows a long book without pressing a button. It enhances the search form that already works without JavaScript. It waits on design and the product owner answering the live-filtering question, and is built as they answer or dropped if the behaviour is dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript on, typing in the address book list's search field or changing its Type select updates, after a short pause and without a full page load, the table, the results line and the pagination to the matches, with no apply button to press (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-026, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-027; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-067; c-169)

With JavaScript off, the same search field and Type select narrow the list when the search button or Enter submits the form, and the results line and pagination describe the matches (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p2-005; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-053, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-054; c-169)
